transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-08 16:00 EST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jamal (Redwood SE), Priya (BlueHorizon Head of ML), Ethan (BlueHorizon Platform), Liam (BlueHorizon PM)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage decomposition, how to map routes to product features for chargeback, and a planning discussion for an initial pilot to validate cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer emphasized need for route-level alerts, SSO and VPC audit log retention requirements, and a clean CSV export for finance.

Topics Covered:
- Route attribution (how to tag routes and map to product features)
- Per-route token cost breakdown and cost-per-call metrics
- Console dashboards: filters, cohorting, and custom routes
- Alerts, SLOs, and anomaly detection for spend spikes
- Security and deployment constraints (VPC peering, KMS, SOC2 docs)
- Next steps for pilot and data needed from BlueHorizon

Action items (recap in call):
- Maya to enable sandbox org, share quickstart + demo deck
- Jamal to prepare baseline per-route cost worksheet + sample script
- BlueHorizon to send traffic profile and internal route map

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, really appreciate you scheduling this. um today Jamal and I will run through the console — focusing on usage decomposition per route and how you can get cost attributions to product teams.
[00:18] Priya (BlueHorizon): thanks Maya, excited. we want something that lines up to our billing team and product owners. latency and cost are both important but finance needs a clean export.
[00:28] Jamal (Redwood SE): yup totally. quick note — our per-route view ties each request path to a route id you can set via SDK header or tag in the proxy. then the console shows token counts, p50/p95 latency, and estimated billed cost per route.
[00:41] Ethan (BlueHorizon): what about partial matches? our front end sometimes funnels several logical calls to one endpoint, will we be able to split those?
[00:52] Jamal: short answer yes, you can either add sub-route tags or use the route mapping rules in the console, there's a small regex-based mapping layer. it's not perfect but works for most.
[01:05] Liam (BlueHorizon): can we demo that? like show a sample rule?
[01:10] Jamal: sure give me a sec — pulling up the console now.
[01:22] [screen share starts, occasional background typing noises]
[01:30] Jamal: ok here's the routes page. top left filter you can pick time window and group by route, model, or customer tag. i'm going to toggle group by route then show cost per 1k tokens. see how this deck renders per-route spend, estimated token cost and token breakdown?
[01:50] Priya: mmhmm i see p50 latency next to cost, that's handy. how do you compute the estimated cost? is it tied to the real invoice or a model?
[02:02] Maya: good question — estimated cost uses the customer's pricing profile (hosted per-token rates or dedicated capacity amortized) and the token counts in the trace. it's intended for internal showback/chargeback, not the final external invoice necessarily.
[02:20] Ethan: ok so for dedicated we can set a fixed per-token amortization?
[02:25] Jamal: yep you configure your reserved capacity/amortization policy in settings; the console uses that to compute per-route unit economics.
[02:34] [00:03 faint crosstalk — someone typing]
[02:40] Priya: any way to tie this data back into our billing system? CSV? API?
[02:46] Jamal: both — export to CSV from any view, and we have a usage export API that gives per-route daily aggregates. you can schedule monthly exports too.
[02:58] Liam: great. and for alerts, like if a route spikes in spend overnight, can we get a webhook?
[03:06] Maya: yes alerts can be configured per-route with thresholds on cost or latency; they can send webhook, pagerduty, or slack.
[03:12] Priya: about security — our security team requires SOC2 type II and a KMS for key management, and we need audit logs retained for 1 year. can you handle that?
[03:23] Jamal: we have SOC2 docs and our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS (HSM integration) and configurable audit log retention for the private plane. hosted customers get standard retention but we can discuss extended retention as an add-on.
[03:36] Ethan: hmm we need VPC peering so logs don't leave our network, is that possible?
[03:40] Maya: yep our Private option supports VPC peering and on-prem connectors; for hosted we offer VPC egress controls but full peering is available in Private deployments.
[03:48] [04:00 transition — Jamal clicks into a route detail view]
[04:05] Jamal: here's a route detail — you can see a sample request trace, token usage at each step, embeddings vs generation token split, and model variants used. note the KV cache hit rate shows up — that helps explain cost differences on repeated prompts.
[04:22] Priya: kv cache hit rate... good to know, our FAQ engine should benefit. can you show comparing two similar routes side-by-side?
[04:31] Jamal: yep split-view coming up — selecting two routes. see the delta column with % difference for token cost and p95 latency. you can also pin a baseline period and compare.
[04:45] Liam: do you have any built-in recommendations for optimizing cost? like suggest batching or quantization?
[04:51] Maya: that's in Redwood Optimize — the console surfaces suggestions: batching windows, quantized model variants, and cache hints. we can export recommended settings per route.
[05:02] Ethan: can optimize run a simulation to show projected savings if we change batch size?
[05:07] Jamal: there's a simulation tool in the sandbox — it takes a traffic profile and runs a synthetic batching simulation to estimate savings and latency impact. it's not 100% exact but helpful for planning.
[05:18] [05:20 silence, someone scribbling notes]
[05:25] Priya: all right two concerns: one, we need per-route cost mapped to product teams for chargeback; two, finance wants a reconciliation to our actual invoice at month end. how do others do reconciliation?
[05:38] Maya: recommended approach is to use the usage export API with daily aggregates per route and then join with the invoice line items — our per-route estimate uses the configured pricing profile so it should reconcile within rounding differences. for dedicated, you can amortize reserved cost and apportion by token usage.
[05:55] Priya: any known gotchas?
[05:58] Jamal: watch for model fallback behavior — if a route falls back to a larger model during degraded capacity, cost jumps. we log fallbacks and surface them in the route timeline but you'll want to set fallback policies to control that.
[06:12] Liam: is fallback automatic? can we opt out?
[06:15] Maya: fallbacks are policy-driven; you can pin route to a model version or allow fallback tiers. for production SLAs most teams pin to a compatible smaller model and allow fallback only to lower-cost variants.
[06:28] Ethan: regarding metrics retention — does the console keep per-request traces beyond 30 days? we have regulatory needs for 90 days of trace-level telemetry.
[06:36] Jamal: hosted default is 30 days, extended retention is an enterprise add-on — Private gives you full control over retention.
[06:44] Priya: ok that's a must for us, likely Private deployment.
[06:48] [06:50 short pause]
[06:52] Jamal: switching to a drilldown on anomalies. console can auto-detect spend anomalies using historical baselines and surface which routes drove the delta. you can click from anomaly to raw traces to debug.
[07:05] Priya: can we get automatic root cause suggestions? like say route A spiked because cache warmed down?
[07:12] Jamal: currently we flag correlated signals — cache miss rate, model fallback frequency, and request size. we provide suggested hypotheses, but human review is recommended.
[07:25] Liam: about integration — our product analytics team uses Snowflake. can we push the per-route exports into Snowflake?
[07:33] Maya: yes you can send the scheduled CSVs to an S3 bucket we write to, and then your ETL can pull into Snowflake. we also have a direct connector for some pipelines.
[07:44] Ethan: what about data residency in EU? some of our users are EU-only, need region-specific storage.
[07:51] Jamal: you can pin region per workspace; for Private you control physical region. Hosted has EU regions and we can discuss contractual data residency terms.
[07:59] Priya: any examples of companies doing per-team chargebacks with this?
[08:04] Maya: we have customers in fintech and adtech doing per-product line chargebacks. typically they use route tags and daily exports for finance.
[08:13] Liam: walk me through a concrete example — let's say HelpCenter search route — how do I go from raw logs to a $ value per ticket?
[08:21] Jamal: map each request to route id 'help_search', export daily aggregate tokens for that route, multiply by per-token cost (or amortized reserved cost), add any model-specific fees, then divide by ticket count from your product analytics — easy to automate with the export.
[08:39] [08:40 brief pause — background typing]
[08:44] Priya: we need a sample CSV that shows columns exactly as you'll provide them (date, route_id, tokens_generated, tokens_received, model_name, est_cost_usd). can you include that in the sandbox?
[08:55] Maya: yes we'll include an example CSV schema and a one-week sample export.
[09:02] Ethan: pilot size — what baseline do you suggest we test?
[09:06] Jamal: start with a two-week pilot for the top 10 routes by traffic. run the simulation, gather reconciliation, validate alerts, then iterate.
[09:15] Priya: timeline — we'd like pilot by mid-November.
[09:18] Maya: sounds good, mid-November kickoff, we'll target 11/16 for the 30m pilot kickoff.
[09:24] [09:30 screen switch to Optimize panel]
[09:31] Jamal: last piece — Optimize suggestions per route. here is an example suggestion for batching: suggests moving to burst batching with 50ms window for route X which would save approx 12% tokens with ~10ms added latency. toggling that suggestion shows a projected saving chart.
[09:52] Liam: can we programmatically apply suggestions?
[09:55] Jamal: suggestions are exported; applying may require code changes in your proxy or calling library. we don't auto-change customer traffic.
[10:02] Priya: security check — vendor assessment will ask for SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning, is that available?
[10:09] Maya: yes SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning supported for enterprise workspaces. we'll share the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints in the security packet.
[10:18] Ethan: any performance differences between hosted and private?
[10:22] Jamal: hosted is multi-tenant but optimized; Private/Dedicated gives predictable latency and throughput with less noisy neighbors and custom kernel selection. depends on your latency SLOs.
[10:33] Priya: ok finance question — if we do Reserved Dedicated vs Hosted, can you show us the math for per-token amortization?
[10:40] Maya: yes Jamal has a reserved capacity worksheet he can share; it shows how commit size, amortization period, and utilization impact per-token price.
[10:50] Jamal: i'll attach a sample sheet with scenarios.
[10:54] [11:00 short wrap-up rhythms]
[11:02] Maya: recap: we'll send sandbox access + CSV example, Jamal will share cost worksheet and simulation steps, BlueHorizon will provide traffic sample and route map. schedule 30m pilot kickoff for week of 11/15, preferably 11/16.
[11:18] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:22] Ethan: thanks all, looking forward.
[11:25] Liam: thanks.
[11:30] Maya: thanks team, we'll follow up via email with links and the deck.

Post-call notes:
- Customer repeatedly asked for Private deployment due to retention and VPC peering needs — mark as high priority for the AE.
- Finance needs CSV schema and reconciliation example; include sample recon script in sandbox docs.
- Pilot scope: top 10 routes, 2-week data collection, run Optimize simulation, verify alerts and export plumbing.

End of transcript.
